gaps.explanation: 'Due to personal reasons' is the standard collocation for giving a cause.

gaps.sentence: No sooner had the applause died ___ the encore began.
gaps.explanation: 'No sooner... than' is invariable; 'when' would be wrong here.

gaps.sentence: She kept every receipt ___ she could claim the expenses back.
gaps.explanation: 'So that + could' expresses purpose; 'in case' expresses precaution.

gaps.sentence: ___ it rains all weekend, the ceremony will still be held outdoors.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a possible (not yet real) condition.

gaps.sentence: ___ the fact that the road was icy, the bus kept its usual speed.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite the fact that + clause' concedes a full clause after a preposition.

gaps.sentence: I noted down the reference number ___ I needed it later.
gaps.hint: just in case it proved necessary
gaps.explanation: 'In case' = because it might be needed later; no purpose is intended.

gaps.sentence: It sounds ___ the negotiations are close to a breakthrough.
gaps.explanation: 'It sounds as though...' reports an impression.

gaps.sentence: I enjoyed the film; the ending was weak, ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Though' can come at the end of a sentence as a casual contrast marker; the others cannot.
